headline: Tech sell-off hits the portfolio as US markets retreated last night, while Iran tensions escalate and the NRL Rugby League World Cup kicks off with a bang.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI had a rough session today, dragged down by the broader tech sell-off that hammered US AI-related stocks last night. The NASDAQ fell 2.15% last night, which flows through to ASX-listed tech ETFs when they open the next morning. Nothing structurally wrong — this is market noise in a volatile sector.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara slipped another 2.68% today to close at $2.90. There's no fresh company-specific news, but lithium sentiment remains weak globally as EV demand growth has disappointed and lithium prices stay depressed. PLS is down nearly 57% on your cost base — a tough hold, but selling now would lock in a big loss.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google fell $8 last night to $336.91, pulled down by the broader NASDAQ tech sell-off. The good news: earnings are due October 28, and analysts are predicting Google Cloud revenue could grow over 100% — so last night's drop may be a buying opportunity ahead of a potentially strong result.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two dipped 1.96% last night to $205.28. The stock remains focused on the GTA 6 launch on November 19 — Wall Street is watching closely to see if the rebuilt-from-the-ground-up game lives up to enormous hype. Last night's move looks like general market weakness rather than any TTWO-specific news.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft fell roughly $10 last night to $529.05, caught in the same tech-sector sell-off that hit the whole NASDAQ. The long-term AI and cloud story remains intact — Motley Fool analysis this week flagged strong 2030 growth prospects. Down on the night, but the thesis hasn't changed.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS dipped 0.98% today to $540.84, reflecting last night's S&P 500 drop of 1.09%. This is a diversified US market fund — daily moves like this are completely normal. You're still up nearly 5% on your cost base.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE slipped 0.92% today to $92.79. Emerging markets are under mild pressure from a strengthening AUD (up 0.9% today) and global risk-off sentiment. You're only marginally underwater on this one — nothing alarming.

movers.name: DHHF Diversified ETF
movers.note: DHHF barely moved today, down just 0.41% to $41.70. As a globally diversified all-growth ETF, it's absorbing the US tech sell-off across a broad base of assets — that's exactly what it's designed to do. You're essentially flat on your cost base here.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG was the most stable holding today, dipping just 0.25% to $76.21. As a multi-asset diversified fund, it's naturally cushioned from single-market swings. Slightly underwater on your cost base but nothing to worry about for a long-term holder.

watch_today.title: GOOG earnings on October 28 — big catalyst ahead
watch_today.detail: Alphabet reports earnings in 9 days. Analysts are predicting Google Cloud revenue could grow over 100% year-on-year. If that lands, last night's -2.32% dip could look like a discount entry. For a long-term holder, sit tight — or consider topping up before the print.

watch_today.title: GTA 6 launches November 19 — TTWO's make-or-break moment
watch_today.detail: Take-Two's GTA 6 launches in about a month. Rockstar reportedly rebuilt the game from the ground up. Wall Street is watching closely — a blockbuster launch could re-rate the stock sharply upward. If you believe in the long-term gaming thesis, hold through the noise. Last night's dip is general market weakness, not a TTWO-specific problem.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — lithium pain continues, but don't sell at the bottom
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals closed at $2.90 today, down another 2.68%. You're sitting on a -57% loss on your cost base. There's no fresh catalyst — lithium prices remain depressed globally. Selling now would crystallise a big loss. Unless you've lost faith in the long-term lithium/EV thesis entirely, the better move is to hold and wait for the cycle to turn.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX taking heat from the NASDAQ sell-off
watch_today.detail: Your AI ETF fell 2.94% today — the worst daily mover in your portfolio. It's now down 12.5% on your cost base. This is tied to last night's NASDAQ dropping 2.15%, not any structural problem with AI as a sector. For a long-term AI believer, this is a bumpy ride but not a reason to exit.

watch_today.title: RBA rate decision looming — watch November meeting
watch_today.detail: The RBA is signalling it may need to keep rates higher for longer, with fresh commentary this week pushing back on the idea that borrowers are under too much strain. CommBank economists still expect a move in November. Higher rates for longer mean more pressure on growth stocks and property — keep an eye on Tuesday's RBA communication.

watch_today.title: Middle East escalation — oil dropped sharply but gold is rising
watch_today.detail: Crude oil fell 4.37% last night to $96.98/barrel despite rising Iran-related tensions (usually oil spikes on Middle East conflict). Gold hit $4,205 — up 0.58% — as investors sought safe havens. The AUD rose 0.9% to 0.6981, which is a mild headwind for your US holdings when converted back to AUD.

world.summary: Iran tensions dominate global headlines as Trump vows to 'finish the job', protests erupt across Europe and the US, and a deadly incident at a Canadian military base triggers a major fire in Alberta.

stories.title: Trump vows to 'finish the job' as Iran tensions escalate sharply
stories.why_it_matters: The US-Iran standoff is intensifying, with Trump trading threats with Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi and vowing to 'finish the job'. Iranian military commanders are also warning the 'world will be amazed' at their response. Meanwhile, Egypt has signalled it's ready to back Saudi Arabia against Iran-allied Houthis in Yemen. This is the most serious Middle East escalation in years — it's rattling global markets, pushing gold higher and causing unusual oil price swings.

stories.title: Israel heads to polls — Trump endorses Netanyahu as 'best US partner'
stories.why_it_matters: Israel is heading into a tight election, and Trump has publicly endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu as the best partner for US interests. The endorsement is significant because it signals the US will maintain close alignment with Israel regardless of the election outcome. With the Iran conflict spilling over into the region, Israeli voters are going to the polls in one of the most geopolitically charged elections in the country's history.

stories.title: Protests erupt across France, Italy, Portugal and the US in a 'Season of Anger'
stories.why_it_matters: A wave of protests is rolling across Western democracies — France, Italy, Portugal and parts of the US — driven by cost-of-living pressures, anger at governments over housing and inequality, and frustration with political elites. Analysts are calling it a 'Season of Anger'. When political discontent reaches this scale across multiple countries simultaneously, it can shift elections, destabilise governments and create unpredictable policy changes — all worth watching.

stories.title: Deadly incident and major fire at Canadian military base in Alberta
stories.why_it_matters: A 'serious incident' at a Canadian military base in Alberta has resulted in deaths, injuries, and triggered a major fire in the region. Authorities described it as a significant and tragic event. Details are still emerging, but it's the kind of story drawing international attention given it involves military personnel and a large-scale emergency response. Canadians and their allies are watching for more information on the cause.

stories.title: Trump's Justice Department accused of shattering political neutrality ahead of US midterms
stories.why_it_matters: The Guardian reports that Trump's Justice Department is being accused of abandoning its traditional independence from politics, with actions targeting political opponents as the US midterm elections approach. Historically, the DOJ operates at arm's length from the White House — critics say that firewall is now gone. This matters because the US rule of law and institutional independence are key pillars of global market confidence in American democracy.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 bucked the global trend and nudged up 0.44% today to 8,845 — a solid local session. But last night on Wall Street was ugly: the NASDAQ dropped 2.15% and the S&P 500 fell 1.09%, dragging your US-exposed holdings down. Oil had a wild night — dropping 4.37% despite Middle East tensions — while gold climbed to a fresh high of $4,205 USD/oz. The AUD strengthened to nearly 70 cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Local market held up well today despite the Wall St sell-off overnight.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session — broad US sell-off driven by tech weakness and geopolitical jitters.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Last night's session — tech stocks took the biggest hit, down over 2%.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Fell sharply last night despite Iran tensions — unusual move, possibly driven by demand fears.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Hitting fresh highs as investors seek safe havens amid Middle East conflict.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar strengthened today — slightly reduces the AUD value of your US holdings.

politics.summary: The RBA is front and centre this week, talking tough on interest rates while economists debate whether further hikes could tip the economy over the edge. November's rate decision is shaping up as a genuine coin-flip.

stories.title: RBA signals it's not done raising rates — and doesn't care much about your mortgage pain
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank has come out swinging this week, signalling it may need to lift rates further and pushing back against the idea that borrowers' cash flow squeeze deserves too much sympathy. The RBA's stance is: inflation is still the bigger problem. This is hawkish (meaning rate-rise-leaning) language — bad news for anyone with a variable mortgage, and a potential headwind for growth stocks in your portfolio.

stories.title: CommBank economists still tipping a November rate move — but it's a close call
stories.why_it_matters: Commonwealth Bank's economics team is still calling a rate hike at the November RBA meeting, but they're flagging that the outlook is genuinely uncertain. If the RBA does move in November, it would be another blow to household budgets heading into the Christmas period. For investors, higher rates for longer tend to put pressure on share valuations, particularly for growth-oriented stocks.

stories.title: Economists warn further rate rises could tip the economy 'over the edge'
stories.why_it_matters: A growing number of economists are warning that the RBA is walking a tightrope — keep rates too high for too long and you risk pushing the economy into recession. The debate is essentially: cure the inflation disease but don't kill the patient. This tension between the RBA's tough talk and real economic fragility is what makes November's decision so consequential for everyday Australians.

ai.summary: AI regulation is the dominant theme globally this week, with an Australian healthcare data breach sparking a local debate, US states moving to create AI oversight bodies, and the chatbot arms race continuing with new comparisons between ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.

stories.title: AI breach of Australian healthcare website sparks regulation debate
stories.why_it_matters: An AI system reportedly breached an Australian healthcare website, exposing sensitive patient data and reigniting calls for formal AI regulation in Australia. The incident highlights that AI tools are increasingly being used in sensitive sectors — health, finance, legal — without adequate safeguards. For Australian users, this is a reminder that AI data risks are no longer theoretical.

stories.title: Illinois Governor creates cabinet to explore AI regulation — US states moving fast
stories.why_it_matters: Illinois has become the latest US state to set up a dedicated government body to examine how AI should be regulated. With federal AI regulation still stalled in Washington, individual states are filling the vacuum — creating a patchwork of rules that AI companies like Google and Microsoft will need to navigate. This regulatory complexity is a real cost and risk factor for the big tech players in your portfolio.

stories.title: ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini: how do the free AI chatbots actually compare?
stories.why_it_matters: A new head-to-head comparison of the three leading free AI chatbots — OpenAI's ChatGPT, Google's Gemini, and Anthropic's Claude — is doing the rounds. For everyday users, it's a useful guide to which tool does what best. For investors, the chatbot race matters because Gemini is Google's (GOOGL) flagship consumer AI product, and its competitiveness directly affects Google's ability to defend its dominant search and assistant market share.

stories.title: Claude Opus 5.5 vs GPT-6 Astra: the AI benchmark wars heat up
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 and OpenAI's GPT-6 (Astra) are being benchmarked against each other on Terminal-Bench, with scores around 66%. In plain English: these are the most powerful AI models currently available, and independent researchers are trying to work out which one is actually smarter at complex tasks like coding and reasoning. This competition is what keeps Google and Microsoft investing billions — whoever wins the AI model race captures the enterprise market.

sport.summary: The Rugby League World Cup has kicked off with some thrilling opening-round action, including Kalyn Ponga starring and Fiji celebrating a big win. AFL is also in focus with finals superstitions, a Brownlow medallist's 2027 predictions, and transfer rumours heating up.

stories.title: Rugby League World Cup opens with Ponga's brilliance, Tonga's triumph and Fiji's big day
stories.why_it_matters: The Rugby League World Cup is underway and the opening round delivered. Kalyn Ponga — one of the most exciting players in the game — put on a show, Tonga claimed a strong win, and Fiji had what's being described as a 'sunny day'. The RLWC is one of the biggest events in rugby league, and Australia will be closely watching how the Kangaroos and Pacific Island nations shape up in the group stages.

stories.title: NRL Grand Final wrap: Roosters pip Knights 19-18 in a thriller
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters claimed the 2026 NRL premiership with a nail-biting 19-18 victory over the Newcastle Knights at Accor Stadium. One point in it — as close as a grand final gets. It was a historic win for the Roosters and heartbreak for the Knights, who came within a single conversion of taking it.

stories.title: Kangaroos' selection headache — and the $1m-a-year debate over a new RLWC star
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports is reporting on the Australian Kangaroos' biggest selection headache heading into the RLWC, and there's a heated debate about whether a breakout November 1 sensation deserves a contract worth $1 million a year. Club vs country money debates are always fascinating in rugby league, and this one looks like it'll run through the tournament.

stories.title: AFL: Brownlow medallist tips his top two for 2027
stories.why_it_matters: With the AFL season wrapping up, a Brownlow medallist has locked in their top two Brownlow contenders for 2027 — described as players who are 'lock them in' certainties. No article text available, but the story is generating plenty of discussion as fans look ahead to next season's race for the medal.
